questions.question: What are the limitations on withdrawals?
questions.answer:
The limitations on withdrawals include the following conditions:

1. The minimum standard withdrawal amount is ten (10) USD. If a client's balance is less than ten (10) USD, they can choose to "Unfollow" the Strategy and withdraw the entire balance to their Account [Copy trading TC(1).txt#109@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9].

2. For withdrawals from Cent, Premium, Raw, Pro, and Pro Plus accounts, the following conditions must be met:
   - Withdrawal requests must not cause the margin level of a Trading Account to fall below 150% during weekdays.
   - Withdrawal requests must not cause the margin level of a Trading Account to fall below 300% during weekends and volatile times [Account opening agreement(1).txt#109@db975ecc10394c498d9fce5c4b8cab12].

3. If a withdrawal request does not meet the requirements specified, it will not be accepted [Account opening agreement(1).txt#110@db975ecc10394c498d9fce5c4b8cab12].
questions.ground_truth: Withdrawals should be made using the same method used by the Client to fund his/ her Account and to the same remitter. The Company reserves the right to decline a withdrawal with specific payment method and suggest another payment method where the Clientneeds to proceed with a new withdrawal request, or request further documentation while processing the withdrawal request. If the Company is not satisfied with any documentation provided by the Client will reverse the withdrawal transaction and deposit the amount back to the Client’s Account. More details on the circumstances which the Company might cancel a withdrawal request can be found on “Withdrawal Conditions” which is accessible via the Company’s website.

questions.question: What is a leverage and how can i change it?
questions.answer:
Leverage is a financial tool that allows a client to control a larger position in the market with a smaller amount of capital. It essentially amplifies both potential gains and potential losses.

You can change the leverage of each trading account in your Client Area. According to the context provided, you can adjust the leverage up to five times without any additional requests. If you wish to change it more than five times, you need to send a request to tradingdesk@hfm.com. For demo accounts, you can change the leverage as many times as you want. Additionally, there are no restrictions on increasing leverage, but decreasing leverage is allowed under certain conditions, such as if the margin is zero or if the margin level exceeds 100% [Account opening agreement(1).txt#131@db975ecc10394c498d9fce5c4b8cab12][Client agreement(1).txt#158@95e450ef44aa49f980a3fe0a51cd2e2e].
questions.ground_truth: Leverage is a ratio of amount used in a transaction to the required deposit.A Client can change the leverage within his Client Area of each trading account up to five (5) times. For changing more than five (5) times the Client needs to send a request at tradingdesk@hfm.com. The Company has the option at its own discretion to disable this option. A Client can change the leverage on demo accounts as many times as he wants. A Client has no restrictions to increase the leverage; however, the Company reserves the right to impose restrictions at its sole discretion. A Client is allowed to decrease the leverage in the following cases:(a) If margin is zero;(b) If margin is more than zero and the margin level is more than 100%. A Client may adjust the leverage of each Trading Account up to thirty (30) times via their Client Area. For changes exceeding thirty (30) times, the Client must submit a request to support@hfm.com

questions.question: Will my account be archived any time?
questions.answer: Yes, your account may be archived if there is no financial and/or trading activity and no pending orders for a set period of 60 calendar days. Additionally, any pending orders older than 90 days will be deleted when the account is archived [Account opening agreement(1).txt#133@db975ecc10394c498d9fce5c4b8cab12].
questions.ground_truth:
A trading Account, that is not a cent trading account, shall be archived if the following occurs:(a) No financial and/or trading activity and no pending orders for a set period of 60 (sixty)calendar days. (b) A Trading Account with no financial and/or trading activity for 60 (sixty) days shall be archived and any pending order older than 90 (ninety) days shall be deleted.(c) A Trading Account with no financial and/or trading activity for 60 (sixty) days and pending orders less than 90 (ninety) days, shall be archived when the said pending orders reach 90 (ninety) days and shall be deleted.(d) A Trading Account with equity less than 1$ no financial and/or trading activity for 45 days shall be archived and any pending orders shall be deleted. A Cent Trading Account shall be archived upon the occurrence of any of the following circumstances:a) No financial and/or trading activity (excluding pending orders) has been conducted on the Cent Trading Account for a continuous period of fifteen (15) calendar days and the Account Balance is less than 100 USc. b) No financial and/or trading activity (excluding pending orders) has been conducted on the Cent Trading Account for a continuous period of thirty (30) calendar days, and the Account Balance is equal to or greater than 100 USc.
c) Upon the occurrence of either of the above, the Cent Trading Account shall be archived,and any pending orders shall be automatically deleted.Remaining balance in the Trading Account which will be Archived, shall be transferred to the wallet balance before the Trading Account is archived.Any Trading Account can be classified by the Company as an Archived, regardless of the remaining balance of the Trading Account. A Client can request to restore an Archived Account by sending an email at support@hfm.com . An Archived Account is not considered as a terminated trading account, however, any trading account may only be restored at the Company’s discretion.

questions.question: How does high leverage affect trading risk?
questions.answer: High leverage allows traders to hold positions much larger than their actual account value, which can magnify both losses and profits. This means that while high leverage can increase potential gains, it also significantly increases the risk of substantial losses, potentially exceeding the initial margin funds and any additional deposits made to maintain open positions. If the market trend goes against the trader, they may sustain a total loss of their margin funds [Risk disclaimer (1).txt#6@a980eeae471d4efe8b3b92e8bd478bd5][Trading and Execution .txt#24@0b2d6d6b81274968950b05ecb72f95c4].
questions.ground_truth: High leverage magnifies both profits and losses and can result in losses up to or even exceeding deposits or margin.

questions.question: My Stop Loss was set at a specific price, but major news caused the market to gap through that level. Does HFM have to execute my Stop Loss exactly at the requested price?
questions.answer: No, HFM does not have to execute your Stop Loss exactly at the requested price. Market conditions or technological limitations may make it impossible to execute such orders at the declared price. Once a Stop Loss order is triggered, it turns into a market order, which may be filled at the next best price, potentially resulting in a worse execution than the stipulated price. This means that realized losses can be larger than expected [Risk with CFDS 2.txt#42@6d5ed3fabfc740f0af7c78e3a06][General risk disclosure(1).txt#35@e2d37ef877634605a9f433ae10739688].
questions.ground_truth: No. During news, gaps, volatility or insufficient liquidity, the order may be executed at the first available price and slippage may occur.

questions.question: If I give HFM a specific instruction for executing an order, can that instruction affect the normal best-execution process?
questions.answer: Yes, if you give HFM a specific instruction for executing an order, that instruction may prevent the Company from taking the steps designed to obtain the best possible result for the execution of those orders. The Company will execute the order in accordance with your specific instructions, which satisfies its obligation to provide you with best execution [Order execution policy(1).txt#45@4967f7dae41f449582adf68373bf4720].
questions.ground_truth: Yes. A specific client instruction may prevent HFM from applying some of its normal best-execution procedures for the elements covered by that instruction.

questions.ground_truth: No. HFM's policies state that spreads may widen significantly during news events because of increased volatility and reduced liquidity.

questions.question: My internet connection became unstable and my market order reached HFM with an outdated price. What may happen?
questions.answer: If your internet connection became unstable and your market order reached HF Markets (HFM) with an outdated price, the order might be declined by the Company. This is due to the possibility of sending out-of-date market orders caused by connectivity issues, which can result in poor or interrupted connectivity [Order execution policy(1).txt#24@4967f7dae41f449582adf68373bf4720].
questions.ground_truth: HFM may update the price and execute the order at the best available market price.

questions.question: After the 25th day of Shield 500, I withdraw 40 percent of my available withdrawable funds. What percentage of my applicable Shield bonus may be removed?
questions.answer: If you withdraw 40% of your available withdrawable funds after the 25th day, then 40% of your applicable Shield bonus may be removed as well, since the bonus removal is proportional to the percentage of the withdrawal amount [Shield 500.txt#9@3937dd92ecdc4543b27f7480dad1caea].
questions.ground_truth: 40 percent of the applicable bonus may be removed because bonus removal is proportional to the percentage withdrawn.

questions.question: Can I withdraw the Shield 500 bonus itself as cash?
questions.answer: No, the Shield 500 bonus cannot be withdrawn as cash. It is for trading purposes only and cannot be withdrawn under any circumstances. Only profits earned and the Client’s deposits into the Account may be withdrawn [Shield 500.txt#8@3937dd92ecdc4543b27f7480dad1caea].
questions.ground_truth: No. The bonus is only for trading purposes. Client deposits and earned profits may be withdrawn, but the bonus itself cannot be withdrawn.

questions.question: A Copy Trading follower has 400 USD equity, the Strategy Provider has 5000 USD equity and the follower selects 100 percent Volume Allocation. What is the Copy Ratio?
questions.answer:
The Copy Ratio is calculated as the equity ratio between the Follower and the Strategy Provider multiplied by the chosen Follower Volume Allocation. 

In this case, the calculation would be:

Copy Ratio = (Follower Equity / Strategy Provider Equity) x Volume Allocation
= (400 / 5000) x 100/100
= 0.08

Therefore, the Copy Ratio is 0.08. [Copy trading TC(1).txt#122@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9]
questions.ground_truth: The Copy Ratio is 0.08, calculated as 400 divided by 5000 multiplied by 100 percent.

questions.question: If the Copy Ratio is 0.08 and the Strategy Provider opens a 0.50 lot trade, what lot size should be copied to the follower?
questions.answer:
If the Copy Ratio is 0.08 and the Strategy Provider opens a 0.50 lot trade, the lot size that should be copied to the follower is calculated as follows:

0.50 lot (Strategy Provider's trade size) x 0.08 (Copy Ratio) = 0.04 lot.

Therefore, the follower should copy a trade size of 0.04 lot. [Copy trading TC(1).txt#122@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9]

questions.question: Can I manually open my own additional trades inside a Copy Trading Follower Account?
questions.answer: No, you cannot manually open your own additional trades inside a Copy Trading Follower Account. The only modification option available to you is to close the copied trades in your Follower Account [Copy trading TC(1).txt#90@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9].
questions.ground_truth: No. A Follower Account is designed for copied trades. The follower may close copied trades but cannot independently open additional trades in that account.

questions.question: Can one Copy Trading Follower Account follow two Strategy Providers at the same time?
questions.answer: No, a Follower is permitted to follow only 1 (one) Strategy Provider per Follower Account at any given time [Copy trading TC(1).txt#89@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9].
questions.ground_truth: No. A Follower Account may follow only one Strategy Provider at any given time.

questions.question: I used a Stop Loss, so is it impossible for me to lose more than the loss amount I intended?
questions.answer: Using a Stop Loss does not guarantee that you will not lose more than the intended amount. Market conditions or technological limitations may prevent the Stop Loss from executing at the desired price, and once triggered, it turns into a market order that may be filled at a worse price. Therefore, you could sustain larger losses than expected [General risk disclosure(1).txt#35@e2d37ef877634605a9f433ae10739688][Risk with CFDS 2.txt#42@6d5ed3fabfc740f0af7c78e3a06d1c00].
questions.ground_truth: No. Stop Loss orders may execute at a worse price or may not operate as intended because of market conditions or technological limitations.

questions.question: A Strategy Provider has 5000 USD equity. A follower has 400 USD equity and selects 50 percent Volume Allocation. The Strategy Provider opens 0.10 lot. What is the theoretical follower position and what actually happens?
questions.answer:
The theoretical follower position size can be calculated as follows:

1. Calculate the trade copy ratio:
   \[
   \text{Trade Copy Ratio} = \frac{\text{Follower Equity}}{\text{Strategy Provider Equity}} \times \frac{\text{Volume Allocation}}{100} = \frac{400}{5000} \times \frac{50}{100} = 0.04
   \]

2. Calculate the follower position size:
   \[
   \text{Follower Position Size} = \text{Strategy Provider Position Size} \times \text{Trade Copy Ratio} = 0.10 \times 0.04 = 0.004 \text{ lots}
   \]

However, the minimum trade size is subject to the follower's approval and confirmation, and it states that the trade will open with a minimum trade size of 0.01 lot. Therefore, since 0.004 lots is below the minimum trade size, the trade will not be copied unless the follower approves a minimum trade size of 0.01 lot.

In summary, the theoretical follower position is 0.004 lots, but practically, the trade will not be copied unless the follower approves a minimum trade size of 0.01 lot [Copy trading TC(1).txt#123@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9][Copy trading TC(1).txt#124@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9].
questions.ground_truth: The Copy Ratio is 0.04. The theoretical follower position is 0.004 lot. Because this is below the minimum tradable size, it may open at the minimum 0.01 lot subject to the follower's approval and confirmation; otherwise the trade will not be copied.

questions.question: A Copy Trading follower has 1000 USD in profits and 500 USD in losses. The Strategy Provider charges a 25 percent Performance Fee. How much Performance Fee is payable?
questions.answer:
The Performance Fee payable by the Follower is calculated as follows:

Profit = 1000 USD  
Loss = 500 USD  
Performance Fee = 25%

The calculation is:  
(1000 - 500) * 25% = 125 USD

Therefore, the Performance Fee payable is 125 USD. [Copy trading TC(1).txt#128@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9]
questions.ground_truth: 125 USD. The calculation is (1000 - 500) x 25 percent = 125 USD.

questions.question: A follower has 1000 USD in profits and 1200 USD in losses. The Strategy Provider charges a 30 percent Performance Fee. Is any Performance Fee payable?
questions.answer: No, there is no Performance Fee payable. The calculation would be (1,000 - 1,200) * 30% = -60 USD, which means no fee is due to the Strategy Provider for negative performance [Copy trading TC(1).txt#128@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9].
questions.ground_truth: No. The follower has negative net performance, so no Performance Fee is payable.

questions.question: A Strategy Provider already has three open trades when I start following the strategy. Will those three existing trades automatically appear in my Follower Account?
questions.answer: No, the three existing trades will not automatically appear in your Follower Account. Only subsequent trades opened by the Strategy Provider after you start following will be copied to your account. The trades opened prior to your following will not be opened on your Follower Account [Copy trading TC(1).txt#72@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9].
questions.ground_truth: No. Trades opened before you started following the Strategy Provider are not copied. Only subsequent trades are eligible to be copied.

questions.question: The Strategy Provider eventually closed a trade in profit, but my Follower Account was stopped out earlier because I did not have enough margin. Can I claim that the copy service failed simply because the Strategy Provider made a profit?
questions.answer: No, you cannot claim that the copy service failed simply because the Strategy Provider made a profit. The Follower acknowledges and understands that they shall have no right to claim for any losses arising out of their failure to maintain the margin requirement, even if the Strategy Provider was in a profitable position at the time of closing their positions [Copy trading TC(1).txt#74@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9].
questions.ground_truth: No. The follower is responsible for maintaining sufficient margin. A follower can be stopped out because of insufficient margin even if the Strategy Provider's position later becomes profitable.

questions.question: A Strategy Provider opened a trade during a server maintenance interruption. My copied trade opened later at a worse price. Does the Copy Trading Agreement guarantee identical entry price and profit or loss?
questions.answer: No, the Copy Trading Agreement does not guarantee identical entry price and profit or loss. It states that the Company cannot guarantee that an order opened on the Follower’s Account will be executed at the same price as an order on the Strategy Provider’s Account, which may result in differences in execution time, price, profit, and/or loss [Copy trading TC(1).txt#10@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9].
questions.ground_truth: No. Maintenance, server restarts, technical interruptions and temporary system unavailability may delay or prevent copying and can create differences in execution time, price, profit and loss.

questions.question: I deposit 1000 USD into a Copy Trading account and choose a 20 percent Rescue Level. At what equity should it theoretically trigger, and is exactly 200 USD guaranteed to remain?
questions.answer: If you deposit 1,000 USD and choose a 20% Rescue Level, it would theoretically trigger when your equity reaches 200 USD, as that is the amount secured in case of loss. However, it is important to note that due to high volatility, the actual amount that remains may not be exactly 200 USD, as the company is not liable for differences caused by volatile market conditions [Copy trading TC(1).txt#114@68336238a917439b8c3a0db802e35ec9].
questions.ground_truth: The theoretical Rescue Level is 200 USD. However, exactly 200 USD is not guaranteed because high volatility may cause the Rescue Level to trigger above or below the expected amount.

questions.question: I use an Expert Advisor during a major news event. My EA sends an order at one price but it executes at a very different price. Since HFM allows EAs, must HFM guarantee the EA's requested execution price?
questions.answer: No, HFM does not guarantee the EA's requested execution price. The company allows trading via Expert Advisors but does not offer support regarding their installation, implementation, and proper functioning. Additionally, during volatile market conditions, such as major news events, orders may be subject to slippage, meaning they can execute at prices significantly different from the requested price due to market volatility [Trading and Execution .txt#32@0b2d6d6b81274968950b05ecb72f95c4][Trading and Execution .txt#10@0b2d6d6b81274968950b05ecb72f95c4].
questions.ground_truth: No. HFM permits EA trading, but the user is responsible for the EA. News, volatility and insufficient liquidity can also cause slippage and execution at the first or next available market price.
